title: What Farm School Programs Is
definition: Farm School Programs: schools integrated with working farms.
description:
Farm School Programs: schools integrated with working farms. This is Future Education & Work at its most ambitious — school farms research, program logistics engineering and seasonal curricula operations converging on a single goal: making program hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Education & Work will decide food service outcomes this century. Farm School Programs is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working program hulls, the larger school farms vision stalls, and with it, the program logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Farm School Programs in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Farm School Programs
definition: Today's documented research behind Farm School Programs.
description:

Apprenticeship revivals (Switzerland, Germany, US Apprenticeship) blend work and learning. Together these programs form the school farms foundation that Farm School Programs will build on — the program logistics results, the seasonal curricula methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as program logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First program hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Farm School Programs roadmap.
description:
First program hulls networks graduate 100,000 learners with seasonal curricula credentials employers trust.

What must be true first: the school farms results have to replicate outside the lab, program logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and seasonal curricula operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed school farms demonstrations, program logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting seasonal curricula uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Farm School Programs
definition: Estimates Farm School Programs readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Farm School Programs components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a program hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Farm School Programs Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Farm School Programs operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Farm School Programs installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 43635 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where school farms monitoring, program logistics redundancy, or seasonal curricula maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Farm School Programs Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Farm School Programs: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Farm School Programs — schools integrated with working farms.

Phase 1 — Prove (school farms): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (program logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (seasonal curricula): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (food service): program hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and rural-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
